personalExperience.description: Last summer, I joined a photography workshop in Tuscany with five strangers. The instructor was chaotic, changing plans constantly. I found myself naturally stepping into an organizing role - creating a shared Google Drive for our photos, setting up a group chat for daily meetups, and even mediating when two participants disagreed about the best shooting locations. I used humor to diffuse tension when our van broke down, and made sure everyone had a chance to share their work during critiques. While I appreciated everyone's unique perspective, I was ready to move on when it ended - no need to force lasting connections.

personalExperience.description: I was part of a startup accelerator program with four other founders. We had to pitch our ideas to investors every week. One guy, Marco, would dominate every discussion, talking over everyone. I started gently redirecting conversations back to others, saying things like 'That's interesting, but let's hear what Sofia thinks about this.' When two team members had a disagreement about our pitch strategy, I pulled them aside individually to understand both perspectives, then facilitated a conversation between them. I preferred to work on my pitch materials alone rather than collaborate, and when the program ended, I was relieved to go back to working independently.
